description: The authoritative Slovak card / POS terminal / ATM counts and transaction series were not located as a downloadable NBS product; they appear only via ECB payments statistics datasets and via SBA-published card statistics (outside this cell).
It is unknown whether OpenStats and the Makroekonomická databáza expose stable JSON/CSV endpoints behind their dashboards.
Pre-redesign historical payment-system statistics (annual report chapter 'Platobný styk', pre-2009 SKK-era tables) are only reachable as scattered legacy PDFs with no index.
The exact NBS reporting templates (výkazy/hlásenia) that define which card and terminal fields banks must report were not opened in this pass; the ŠZP submission layer is credentialed.
Some NBS statistical subpages (notably SIPS statistics for 2009-2013) exist only in Slovak, while the /en/ tree is otherwise near-parity.
NBS speeches, presentations and Governor/Board-member remarks were not systematically located as a distinct channel; these often disclose payment- and cash-policy direction before publications do.
No RSS/Atom feed or newsletter endpoint was identified for aktuality or the publication series, so the proposed collection method relies on listing diff-crawls.
The completeness of the EN mirror versus the SK tree is unmeasured; some payment/cash commentary is likely SK-only.
Historical depth of the narrative layer (pre-2010 annual-report cash and payment chapters, full Biatec run 1993–2019) has been identified but not inventoried.
NBS narrative frequently reflects ECB/Eurosystem work (e.g. the euro-area consumer payment-habits study referenced in NBS aktuality). The ECB-side originals sit outside this cell.

No CPV code list has yet been fixed for the payments/ATM/cash domain in SK procurement (candidates include 30123400 sorting/counting machines, 30233190 card readers, 66110000 banking services, 79710000 security/cash-in-transit services, 48000000 software).

Key public buyers of card-acceptance and cash services were not individually verified: Sociálna poisťovňa, Štátna pokladnica, Ministerstvo financií SR, Železnice/ZSSK, Bratislava/Košice transport operators, university hospitals.
The concrete TED API endpoint and query syntax for country=SVK plus CPV filtering was not confirmed in this pass; only the TED portal and general dataset references were observed.
The supplier side (cash-in-transit and ATM service firms operating in SK — e.g. security/CIT companies, ATM deployers) was not mapped from award records in this pass.
Below-threshold and small municipal purchases of POS terminals and cash-handling equipment are dispersed across EKS, eGovZmluvy and hundreds of municipal sites.
Terminal/ATM OEM SK channel partners other than Printec (e.g. Diebold Nixdorf's SK entity, Verifone/Ingenico/PAX SK distribution contracts, cash-handling and CIT firms) are not yet enumerated.

Public-procurement surfaces were not covered in this cell: state-owned or state-adjacent institutions (Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka, Exim, Slovenská pošta/365.bank history) do tender banking technology, and those tenders name vendors and quantify volumes.
Vendor reference and case-study pages are undated snapshots; there is no historical series showing when SK deployments started or ended.
Only one hard supplier-side quantification was captured (Global Payments SK: >37,000 terminals, >EUR 2bn annual volume). ATM-side counts by vendor/operator remain unquantified from the supplier side.
Slovak-language searching worked well for integrators and terminal resellers but produced almost nothing for global OEM case studies, which exist only in English and rarely mention Slovakia.
No SK-focused fintech/payments boutique consultancy or acquirer-side advisory identified (equivalent of local payment-strategy shops).

Bank-owned analytical units (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa Analýzy, VÚB / Tatra banka economic research) were not searched this pass; they publish quantified sector commentary and are true analytical intermediaries.
SK academic repositories (CRZP central register of theses, EUBA/UMB/TUKE institutional repositories, Ekonomický časopis archive) not queried.
Rating agency access (Fitch, S&P, Scope) to SK bank sector reports not established.

The flagship Slovak business press — Trend (etrend.sk), Hospodárske noviny (hnonline.sk), Forbes Slovensko (forbes.sk), Aktuality.sk ekonomika, Startitup/Refresher money desks — is not represented by concrete URLs in this slice.
Only TOUCHIT.sk was captured on the IT-trade side; Živé.sk, DSL.sk, Root.sk-equivalents and Netky/HN Tech were not surfaced with concrete payment/ATM articles.
No TV/radio economic programmes (RTVS Ekonomika, TA3 business coverage, Markíza/JOJ news) were assessed, though they routinely air bank spokespeople giving ATM and branch counts.
No archival/back-issue access strategy was established for Slovak media (paywalled archives, press-database aggregators such as Newton Media / Monitora / Slovakia Online).
Hungarian-language media serving southern Slovakia (e.g. Új Szó) were not searched, despite covering local branch/ATM closures in Hungarian-speaking districts.
Acquirer/PSP employer surfaces (Worldline SK, Global Payments/Nexi presence, Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB, 365.bank career pages) were not individually enumerated in this pass.
Conference agendas are ephemeral; past-edition programmes and decks were not archived in this pass.
English-language SK-focused surfaces (expat/IT job boards, EN conference agendas, EN association pages) were only lightly covered relative to sk sources.
Consumer-complaint statistics from Slovenská obchodná inšpekcia (SOI) regarding refusal of cash/card acceptance were not searched.

The actual Wayback capture density for nbs.sk payment/card statistics URLs (how far back, how frequently, whether linked XLS/PDF files were captured or only HTML) is unknown because the archive was unreachable from this agent.

No crosswalk yet exists between retired and current series identifiers across the three continuity breaks identified: ECB PSS → PCP/PMC, ECB SDW nodes → data.ecb.europa.eu dataset keys, and ŠÚ SR DATAcube cube codes → STATdata codes.
The dataset-level inventory of data.gov.sk / data.slovensko.sk for NBS, MF SR and ŠÚ SR under payment/banking keywords was not enumerated in this run.

Nothing found provides machine-readable Slovak payment/card series before roughly 2003 (SIPS) or 2011 (Statistical Bulletin). Koruna-era and early-2000s card/ATM data appear to exist only in paper or scanned form.
Whether NBS OpenStats exposes a stable underlying JSON/XHR data endpoint (as opposed to UI-only export) was not determined.

Slovak-language searching for genuinely archival concepts ('archív štatistík', 'ukončená databáza', 'zrušená stránka') returned mostly current-page results; no Slovak-language index of retired statistical releases was found.

I identified the ECB dataset families relevant to SK (payment card accepting devices, cards and card payments, discontinued annual payments statistics) but did not resolve the concrete SDMX series keys for Slovakia (REF_AREA=SK) for ATM counts, POS terminal counts, or card transaction volumes.

The cell was scoped to ECB/Eurosystem, but adjacent supranational aggregators carrying SK payment/card rows were not explored: Eurostat, the European Payments Council SEPA payment statistics, and the BIS CPMI Red Book statistics.
Slovak-language querying was performed and is documented, but produced no ECB-hosted statistical sources; the SK-language surface for this cell remains thin and untested beyond nbs.sk news items.

Eurosystem cash-side statistics beyond banknote circulation (banknote lodgements/withdrawals at NCBs, cash recycling, ATM withdrawal values in the payments dataset) were not individually enumerated for SK.
This pass was search-driven; no candidate URL was fetched, so access status, robots/ToS posture and any bot defences on data.ecb.europa.eu (a JS-heavy SPA) are untested.

No EU/international aggregator in this cell publishes SK-specific card transaction volumes, POS terminal counts or ATM withdrawal values at national granularity except IMF FAS access points; ECB Payments Statistics (out of this cell) is the only comprehensive SK-level source.
Eurostat, BIS and IMF SDMX endpoints and exact dataset/series identifiers for SK were inferred from portal documentation rather than exercised in this pass.

Cash-usage behaviour (share of POS transactions in cash, cash-holding habits) for SK is not covered by any aggregator in this cell; the closest EU-level instrument is the ECB SPACE study, which sits outside this cell.
data.europa.eu Slovak-language faceted search was identified but not exercised with a full sk keyword set (platobné karty, bankomat, POS terminál, bezhotovostné platby, finančná inklúzia).
EBA/EU-level supervisory data annexes that sometimes carry SK payment-fraud and PSD2 statistics were not explored, as they sit at the boundary of this cell.
Payment-method (cash vs card) breakdown of eKasa receipts is collected by the state but not published.
STATdata canonical URL and API surface unconfirmed; DATAcube cube identifiers for retail turnover and household expenditure not yet enumerated.

Household budget/expenditure statistics (rodinné účty, EU-SILC výdavky domácností) were identified only generically as living in the ŠÚ SR databases; no specific survey page or cube was pinned down in this pass.

Act No. 384/2025 Z. z. on evidencia tržieb (eKasa successor, in force from 1 January 2026) was identified via secondary reporting only; the law text, dôvodová správa and doložka vplyvov were not retrieved, and it is unclear whether it changes what data is published or whether it mandates cashless acceptance.
data.gov.sk and opendata.mfsr.sk were identified as catalogues but were not queried dataset-by-dataset in this pass.
All eKasa open datasets are distributed as XLSX files rather than through an API; the ŠÚ SR portal uses volatile WebSphere URLs.
No SK merchant/retail-side association was scouted in this pass (e.g. retail or e-commerce trade bodies that publish card-acceptance and cash-handling behaviour from the merchant perspective).
SBA's statistics category spans roughly 2018-2026 but only the current release page was inspected; the historical XLSX vintages behind each monthly post were not enumerated.
SBA expert committees (odborné komisie) — where payment, cash and security working groups sit — were not enumerated; committee pages often name bank representatives and publish position papers.
Cash usage is thinly covered at association level: no SK cash-in-transit / cash-handling association or association-published cash-cycle statistics were located.
SBA maintains an English mirror (sbaonline.sk/en/) but it appears thinner than the Slovak site; the extent of English coverage of the statistics section was not measured.
TIPS-specific SK participation and volume reporting (which SK banks reach instant payments via TIPS versus other reachability) was not resolved beyond the NBS SEPA instant-credit-transfer page.

Pillar 3 / NBS Opatrenie 16/2014 disclosure documents were located for ČSOB SK and (an older year for) SLSP, but the current-year disclosure URLs for VÚB, Tatra banka, 365.bank and Prima banka were not individually located in this pass.

POS/merchant-acquiring disclosures were only reached through VÚB's product page. Acquiring in SK is partly handled by specialised arms and processors (e.g. bank acquiring units and third-party processors) whose own disclosures were not searched in this cell.

Each bank operates an official ATM/branch locator ('nájdi bankomat', 'pobočky a bankomaty') which typically has a JSON backend giving an exact live ATM count and geodata; none was probed in this pass.

The cell's named list omits smaller SK-active retail players that also disclose card/client numbers (e.g. Fio banka pobočka, Oberbank, J&T Banka, Privatbanka, ČSOB Stavebná sporiteľňa, Prvá stavebná sporiteľňa), which were seen only as search noise.

Several banks (VÚB, 365.bank, Prima banka) now publish the statutory annual report primarily as ESEF/iXBRL (XHTML), with PDF marked 'neoficiálna/informatívna'. Operational KPIs are in untagged narrative blocks.
English-language mirrors of the Slovak bank reports and newsrooms (e.g. /en/ paths on slsp.sk, vub.sk, csob.sk) were not systematically mapped; only the Erste Group English IR portal was captured.

Card scheme SK-country outputs (Visa CEE / Mastercard Slovakia country press and 'Slovensko platí kartou' style campaigns) were not directly enumerated in this pass, though a VÚB campaign referencing 'Slovakia Pays by Card' surfaced indirectly. Schemes are the usual original source behind SK terminal-density and contactless-share figures quoted by the press.

No cross-check was made against ECB Payments Statistics / NBS payment statistics tables (Štatistika platobného styku), which report SK acquiring-side counts (POS terminals, acceptance points, card transactions at terminals located in SK) on a harmonised basis. This is the authoritative denominator against which every acquirer's self-reported estate should be normalised.

Crypto/e-money hybrids and BNPL providers active in SK (e.g. Fumbi-type EMIs, Twisto/Skip Pay-style BNPL, Revolut Bank's SK merchant activity) were not covered, nor were payroll/expense-card EMIs. These hold e-money licences and appear in the NBS register but sit outside classic card acquiring.

Interchange Fee Regulation (IFR) Article 9/12 disclosures — acquirers' published merchant service charge and scheme-fee breakdowns — were not located for SK acquirers, although Global Payments' 'dôležité dokumenty' and SKPAY's 'obchodné podmienky' PDFs are the likely carriers.

All searching was done in Slovak and English as required. Czech-language sources were only encountered incidentally (paytenpos.cz, Comgate) despite the CZ/SK payments market being operationally integrated — many SK-relevant PSP disclosures are published only in Czech.
Independent ATM deployers beyond Euronet (e.g. bank-outsourced fleets, retail-sited deployers, Slovenská pošta cash-access points) are not yet mapped for SK.
Financial data was found via FinStat (an aggregator with restrictive ToS) rather than the primary Register účtovných závierok / Obchodný register.
Scheme commercial data products (Mastercard Economics Institute / SpendingPulse, Visa Business & Economic Insights) were not individually located for SK coverage.

No Slovak-language term was found or tested for 'independent ATM deployer' as an industry category — SK usage appears to be descriptive ('nezávislý prevádzkovateľ bankomatov') rather than an established term, which weakens recall.
Group-level filings that segment SK/CEE (Euronet Worldwide 10-K ATM counts, Loomis AB annual/interim reports) were identified as useful but not yet retrieved.

Inbound/outbound passporting notices for SK (which EU PIs/EMIs are notified to operate into Slovakia) were not located as a dedicated NBS page; only the EBA register was confirmed as carrying passport data.
All registers found expose current state only; no register was confirmed to publish historical snapshots, so entry/exit dating depends on our own diffing from the first collection date onward.
NBS licence withdrawals, sanctions and enforcement decisions (Vestník NBS / rozhodnutia) were referenced but not pinned to a specific collectable URL in this pass.
ESMA registers (CASP under MiCA, crowdfunding providers) and the EBA credit-institutions register were identified only at hub level, not as SK-filtered endpoints.
Commercial SK company-data vendors (e.g. FinStat and similar) were not evaluated in this pass; they often add computed financial ratios and industry aggregates on top of the public registers.
